set.question: Los padres de Carlos __ tres hijos.

why: Carlos and Ana as parents of three contradicts the story (Carlos has a brother, a sister, no children)
'Mi padre' uses mi before a1-05-02 (possessives)
'tu madre' uses tu before a1-05-02; 'dos hijos' contradicts the story (Carlos's mother has three children)
dos/tres are used from the first lesson (numbers are a1-10-02; 'dos' is listed only at a1-08-02, 'tres' in no list); add them here (rule 6c) or replace every use with un/una
hijos = 'children' is used in grammar examples and exercises (Ana tiene dos hijos; two children) but only 'son' is glossed
'viven' is regular -ir conjugation (Unit 6) used before its screen

old:
"title": "Introducing someone: *este* / *esta*",
      "content": "Use *este* (masculine) or *esta* (feminine) with *es* to introduce a person: \"this is...\". *este*/*esta* agrees with the gender of the person you're introducing, not with your own gender."
new:
"title": "Introducing someone: *él es* / *ella es*",
      "content": "You know *él es* and *ella es* from Unit 2. To introduce a family member, add a possessive: *Ella es mi madre*. *Él* or *ella* depends on the person you are introducing, not on you."
why: screen teaches este/esta (demonstratives, A1 Unit 10) as new; recap Unit 2's él/ella es instead

old:
"spanish": "Esta es mi madre.",
          "english": "This is my mother."
new:
"spanish": "Ella es mi madre.",
          "english": "She is my mother."

old: Use *ser* + adjective to describe people. Adjectives such as *tranquilo* and *divertido* change to agree with gender and number. *Amable* stays the same in the singular.
new: You know *ser* + adjective and agreement from Units 1 to 4: the adjective agrees with the person in gender and number. Here the people are your family. Adjectives such as *tranquilo* and *divertido* change (*tranquila*, *tranquilos*, *tranquilas*); *amable* stays the same in the singular.
why: screen presents ser + adjective agreement as new (A1 Units 3-4)
length-giveaway 9 vs 5; wrong options as long as the right one, met words
